correctness.rationale: For a uniform surface-area point X on the unit cube and vertex o, three adjacent faces have squared geodesic radius u²+v²; an opposite face point (1,y,z) has exact radius² 1+y²+z²+2min(y,z). Two unfolded 2-face paths attain the latter. The source provides a finite exhaustive comparison of 80 simple face walks, reduced to 24 integer coefficient classes each satisfying the necessary affine inequalities at all four chamber vertices; the argument that a shortest path can be shortened if it visits a face twice justifies path reduction. Analytic integration over the incident quarter-disk and two opposite triangles yields the displayed A(r),B(r) and F=(A+B)/2, transitions at 1 and sqrt2 and endpoint sqrt5. Direct rational polynomial integration gives E[R²]=3/2,E[R⁴]=61/18; endpoint rescaling gives 1-F~(5-r²)²/48. Independent numerical integration by Monte Carlo using 45,000 independently generated pairs compared the analytic CDF at 5 radii (errors bounded by 0.006); this corroboration is not proof of metric optimality. Critical exact face-walk code was read and its inequalities traced. No two-random-point formula is asserted. An additional independent, exact integer planar unfolding generator reconstructed all 80 face-simple routes and precisely 24 quadratic coefficient classes and verified all four chamber-vertex inequalities for every class. The corresponding path-completeness proof then establishes the pointwise intrinsic metric, not Monte Carlo.
